transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I’m here because I can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore. I’m a software developer, and it’s gotten really noticeable at work. Like, I’ll be fixing a rendering bug—something that should be pretty straightforward, just tracing through the code—and then a Slack ping comes in, or I notice some weird color pattern on the screen, or there’s a siren outside, and suddenly I’m off in a completely different direction.

It’s not just “oh, I got distracted for a second.” It’s like that one thing pulls me into a whole new idea before I’ve even finished the line of code I was writing. Then I’ll realize I’ve got half a fix open, three browser tabs, some note about a different feature, and I don’t even remember exactly where I was. It’s frustrating because my job depends on being able to hold a problem in my head long enough to solve it, and lately my attention just keeps getting yanked away by every little thing.
Have you noticed yourself acting impulsively or feeling unusually restless or hyperactive lately, like you can't sit still or you're doing things without thinking them through?

Yeah… yes, definitely. It’s like there’s this constant current running through me, like I wake up already in motion mentally before I’ve even gotten out of bed. I’ll open my eyes and I’m already planning code changes, then some new feature idea, then how the interface should look, and then—this sounds random—but I start thinking about how it could be presented, like an exhibition layout almost, or what the press angle would be if it turned into something bigger.

And sitting still just feels… wrong. Like I’m wasting the moment if I’m not doing something with all of it. I’ll be at my desk and instead of just working through one task, I’m bouncing between things, getting up, pacing, opening files, sketching out ideas, sending messages, rearranging notes. It doesn’t always feel bad in the moment, honestly—it can feel productive, like everything is connected and I just need to move fast enough to keep up with it. But then I look back and realize I’ve been acting on things before really thinking them through.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like your work or hobbies?

I don’t know that I’d describe it as down or depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, especially when I can’t finish something cleanly or I realize I’ve made a mess of my workflow, but it doesn’t feel like… sadness sitting on me, if that makes sense.

And I haven’t really lost interest in work or hobbies. If anything, I still get pulled toward them pretty strongly. Maybe too strongly sometimes. But I wouldn’t say I’m not enjoying things or that everything feels flat. It’s more that my attention is hard to manage, not that I don’t care about the things anymore.
